title: Finland – Medical equipments – Blood pressure monitor for toe/ankle and upper arm measurements
description: The HUS Group requests tenders for a device intended for measuring toe/ankle and upper arm blood pressure. The device will be used at the Vascular Surgery Outpatient Clinic (Arterial Laboratory). The Arterial Laboratory performs approximately 5000 ABI (ankle–brachial index) and finger pressure measurements annually. The ABI examination involves measuring blood pressure simultaneously from both upper arms and both ankles. Toe pressures must likewise be comparable with the upper arm pressure measured at the same time. The measurement protocol also includes recording a pulse volume waveform at ankle level. The same device is also used to measure finger pressures. The purpose of the procurement is to replace equipment reaching the end of its service life; therefore, the measurement results of the new device must be comparable with those produced by the devices currently in use in the Arterial Laboratory (Periflux system 6000 peripherial pressure premium). The procurement includes one (1) device and the consumables specific to the device. The procurement also includes the following options: - a maintenance agreement after the warranty period for each device, and - two (2) additional devices and the consumables spesific to the devices The contracting authority will decide on the use of the options by 31 December 2028. The estimated total value of the procurement (VAT 0%) is approximately EUR 300,000. This estimate includes the device, optional devices, device‑specific consumables, and the post‑warranty maintenance agreement. The contracting authority does not commit to the stated euro amounts or the consumption quantities presented in the request for quotation. Final order quantities may be higher or lower than indicated. This is a single procurement and has not been divided into lots. The equipment package constitutes a technically and functionally coherent whole, and dividing it into several procurements would not be appropriate. Splitting the procurement could jeopardize compatibility, functionality, and clarity of responsibilities, thereby significantly increasing risks related to implementation and maintenance. As this is an investment procurement, the Tenderer must commit to delivering the equipment (one) during the year 2026. The subject matter and requirements of the procurement are described in detail in the invitation to tender and its annexes including all key purchasing details.

title: Denmark – Floodgates – Udbud vedrørende anskaffelse af mobilt opdæmningsmateriel
description: Udbud vedrørende anskaffelse af mobilt opdæmningsmateriel Beskrivelse (dansk): Beredskabsstyrelsen ("BRS") ønsker sammen med landets 30 kommunale redningsberedskaber ("de Kommunale Beredskaber") at indgå en rammeaftale om anskaffelse af mobilt dæmningsmateriel i form af fritstående oversvømmelsesbarrierer. Anskaffelsen har primært til formål at understøtte BRS' og de Kommunale Beredskabers akutte håndtering af klimahændelser, herunder ved varsling om forhøjet vandstand fra bagland såvel som havvand, samt ved indsats i forbindelse med større brande. Det mobile dæmningsmateriel skal anvendes både selvstændigt i forbindelse med håndteringen af bl.a. klimahændelser, ligesom det skal indgå som supplement til BRS' og de Kommunale Beredskabers eksisterende opdæmningsmateriel. Materiellet skal kunne anvendes i flere forskellige indsatsscenarier. Det skal for det første kunne etableres hurtigt og fleksibelt over varierende strækninger ved ekstraordinære vandstandsstigninger, herunder ved akut indsats i baglandet, f.eks. ved søer og åer, samt ved kyster og havne. Det skal for det andet kunne benyttes til beskyttelse af enkeltobjekter, f.eks. kritisk infrastruktur. Det skal for det tredje kunne anvendes som vandreservoir i forbindelse med større brandindsatser, hvor vand anbringes i reservoiret, hvorfra én eller flere pumper fordeler vandet til indsatsområdet. Det mobile dæmningsmateriel skal have en primær højde svarende til højden på BRS' eksisterende og mest anvendte opdæmningsmateriel. Da de lokale beredskabers risikovurderinger og behov varierer, ønskes der herudover tilbudt opdæmningsmateriel i andre højder, som muliggør tilpasning til områder med behov for lavere eller højere opdæmning. Det er væsentligt, at materiellet tillader hurtig, let og effektiv transport, etablering og nedtagning, herunder at håndteringen kan ske med et minimum af ressourcer og på en arbejdsmiljømæssigt forsvarlig måde. Materiellet forudsættes at kunne benyttes flere gange. Materiellet vil blive oplagret på lager og transporteret til indsatsområderne via lastbil. Under indsættelse skal materiellet kunne håndteres ved håndkraft, herunder aflæsses, opsættes, nedtages og læsses, af et minimalt mandskab. Rammeaftalen har en varighed af 4 år fra underskrift.

Lisäksi tavoitteena on tukea vammaisen henkilön perheenjäsenten ja muiden läheisten valmiuksia tukea häntä erilaisissa elämäntilanteissa. Tarkoituksena on saada vammaisen henkilön omat kyvyt ja voimavarat täysimääräisesti käyttöön. title: Global Tactical Edge Acquisition Directorate Accelerated Capability Event 27-02- Spectrum Enabled Warfare
description: This SAM notice is to highlight the G-TEAD USAREUR-AF ACE 27-02 Spectrum Enabled Warfare Powered by XTECH. Accelerated Capability Event 27-02 | Spectrum Enabled Warfare See: https://xtech.army.mil/ for official response date. Description: The U.S. Army, through the Global Tactical Edge Acquisition Directorate (G-TEAD) and U.S. Army Europe and Africa (USAREUR-AF), in operational partnership with the U.S. Army FUZE xTech Program, is conducting an Accelerated Capability Event (ACE) to evaluate, demonstrate, and acquire operationally mature (TRL 6+) electromagnetic spectrum operations (EMSO) capabilities. This effort enables U.S. Army forces operating within a North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) and joint coalition framework on the Eastern Flank to sense, understand, exploit, attack, and protect across a contested electromagnetic environment (EME) and connected cyberspace. To preserve combat power and freedom of maneuver, forces must protect tactical command and control (C2) networks while delivering synchronized lethal and non-lethal effects at depth against adversary systems. The G-TEAD Library of Competed Capabilities utilizes Accelerated Capability Events (ACEs) via including, but not limited to, Prize Challenge events (e.g., Army xTech Program) and Alternate Pathway submissions through open call announcements to create a competitive, compliant, and scalable acquisition framework. Vendors who qualify will have their capabilities added to the G-TEAD Library of Competed Capabilities and remain eligible for rapid follow-on contracts, agreements, or Orders without the need for further competition. This SAM notice is to highlight ACE 27-02 Spectrum Enabled Warfare. Selected vendors will receive prize funds, demonstrate solutions in Germany before Army and NATO end-users, may leave behind kits for follow-on operational evaluation, and may be awarded a Prototype Other Transaction (OT) Agreement (10 U.S.C. � 4022) with 10 U.S.C. � 4022(f) � Follow-on Production Contracts or Transactions included. Winners will be onboarded into the G-TEAD Library of Competed Capabilities for potential follow-on procurement following the planned event. In addition, G-TEAD provides funding to ASCC commanders to select winners to purchase capabilities for operational deployment. Goals Accelerate warfighter-relevant technology fielding Ensure statutory competition requirements are satisfied up front, enabling direct ordering. Provide a unified experimentation and operational fielding environment for U.S., NATO, and coalition partners. Enable compliant acquisition pathways to include via FAR, OTs (10 U.S.C. �� 4021, 4022, 4023), BAAs, CSOs, and 10 U.S.C. � 4025 (Prize Competitions). Support Foreign Military Sales (FMS) and Direct Commercial Sales (DCS) for allied/partner nations. Vendor On Ramp Pathways via ACEs: Prize Challenge Pathway: Vendors compete in prize-based challenges (e.g. xTech competition), receive initial prize funding, demonstrate solutions in designated regions, and qualify to onboard into the G-TEAD Library of Competed Capabilities. Alternate Pathway: Future notices will be used to issue calls for Submission via Alternate Pathway. The Alternate Pathway release is PENDING with no announcement date planned at this time. We greatly appreciate the immense interest we have received from the Defense Industrial Base in joining the G-TEAD Library of Competed Capabilities. Please do NOT email or inquire about the Alternate Pathway at this time. No action will be taken if you submit information. We expect to execute multiple ACEs annually. Previous and future efforts can be found at https://xtech.army.mil/competitions/ Capability Focus Areas The Army is seeking innovative capabilities that demonstrate performance in one (1) of four (4) capability areas: � Capability 1: Electromagnetic Support / Tactical Surveillance (*) Passive sensing solutions that detect, characterize, direction-find, and geolocate complex emitters at the tactical edge without producing detectable RF signatures or overloading tactical networks. Emphasizes low-SWaP-C distributed sensor employment across maneuver formations, autonomous edge signal processing, multi-sensor tasking/handoffs under Disconnected, Degraded, Intermittent, or Limited (DDIL) conditions, and cross-mission utility (c-UAS, CIED, ES, and EA). Modalities include mounted, dismounted/static, ground robotics, and Group 1�3 UAS. � Capability 2: Autonomous Network Management (*) Open, self-healing, automated network infrastructures adhering to open standards (MOSA, SOSA, CMOSS / CMFF) capable of autonomously orchestrating distributed EMSO assets, managing dynamic spectrum resources, executing automated PACE plans, and routing critical sensor-to-shooter feeds under DDIL constraints without continuous operator intervention. � Capability 3: Electromagnetic Environment Visualization and Battle Damage Assessment Tools (*) Intuitive, multi-echelon user interfaces translating dense RF environments into real-time operational visual layers. Includes algorithmic automated Non-Lethal Battle Damage Assessment (NL-BDA) capable of measuring and validating the efficacy of deployed electronic attack against target signatures, edge-native analytics, and direct sensor-to-shooter integration with next-generation mission command systems. � Capability 4: Electromagnetic Attack & Active Countermeasures Modular, scalable Electronic Attack (EA) and Counter-C5ISR frameworks across Battalion to Corps echelons. Focuses on platform-tailored SWaP-C scalability (dismounted, vehicle-mounted, robotic/UAS), cognitive closed-loop jamming (sense-and-jam, adaptive protocol disruption), broadband multi-threat defeat (wideband DRFM, protocol injection, synthetic target generation, NAVWAR/GNSS denial/deception), and distributed multi-node cooperative jamming integrated into joint fires networks. (*) Note on SBIR Eligibility: Army SBIR Direct to Phase II (DP2) funding opportunities under topic ARM27BX01-DP001 are strictly limited to eligible U.S. Small Businesses selected as finalists/winners in Capability Areas 1, 2, and 3. Capability Area 4 is strictly ineligible for SBIR funding, but finalists/winners in Capability Area 4 are eligible for direct Prototype Other Transaction Agreements (10 U.S.C. � 4022) and FAR-based procurement contract opportunities.
